title: Built-in Expression Macros
hints: Default arguments like `#function` are evaluated at the **call site**.
Inside `start()`, `#function` is `start()`; the line is where `logged` is called.
jsBridge: `#fileID`, `#function`, `#line` and `#column` are compile-time expression macros, captured at the **call site** when used as default arguments. JS has no equivalent; you'd parse `new Error().stack`.

compass.q: JS logging libraries parse stack traces to get file and line. Why is `#line` as a default argument better?
Why does `logged("x")` report the *caller's* line, not the line inside `logged`?
`#file` vs `#fileID` vs `#filePath`: which leaks your machine's directory structure into a release binary?
`Logger` from `os` records this metadata for you. When would you still pass `#function` yourself?
